text:
All fixed and verified:

- `spiral([[1, 2, 3]])` now returns `[1, 2, 3]`
- The 3×4 matrix returns exactly 12 values, each once: `[1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 11, 10, 9, 5, 6, 7]`
- Edge cases (single element, single column, empty matrix, 2×2, 3×3) all correct, and the input is not modified
- All existing tests pass

The root cause: when the remaining band was a single row (`top == bottom`), the bottom-row loop re-traversed elements already added by the top-row loop; when it was a single column (`left == right`), the left-column loop re-traversed elements already added by the right-column loop. Guarding those two loops with `top < bottom` and `left < right` fixes it.

arguments.summary: Fixed the spiral-order bug in grid/spiral.py: the bottom-row and left-column loops were unconditionally run on each pass, so when the remaining band was a single row (top == bottom) or single column (left == right) they re-emitted elements already collected, causing duplicates for non-square matrice...
